server.name: com.mailbox-mcp/mailbox-mcp
server.description: Read, send, file and search email in any Gmail, Microsoft 365 or IMAP mailbox, plus its calendar.
server.title: Mailbox MCP

com.mailbox-mcp.authentication: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration and PKCE. Mailbox credentials are envelope-encrypted and are never held by the client.
com.mailbox-mcp.summary: Mailbox MCP connects an assistant to a real mailbox over IMAP and SMTP, so it can read, write, file and search mail as the owner would. The mailbox has to look untouched afterwards in Outlook or webmail, and that rule decides the implementation: reading never marks a message as read, a send files exactly one copy in Sent, a delete moves to Trash, a draft is saved where another client can edit it, a move keeps flags and the internal date, and folders resolve by their special-use flag instead of by name. It archives and reports spam by role rather than by folder name, so on Gmail archiving drops the inbox label. It reads attachments: a PDF, a Word file or a spreadsheet as text, a photo as a picture. After a send, check_bounces says whether an address failed for good or is being retried, and check_receipts whether it was opened, even when nothing came back. catch_up, waiting_on and owed_replies answer in one call each what came in, what nobody has answered and who is waiting on a reply. A diary connected as a separate step adds calendar tools: reading and searching events, free/busy, booking and moving your own time, inviting, cancelling, answering or proposing another time, and the out-of-office reply. A CardDAV address book connected to an IMAP mailbox, also separately, lets find_contact read the book beside the mailbox's own history, and adds read_contact to open one card. No contact is stored on the server. A mailbox with no diary or book is handed none of those tools rather than tools that refuse, so the tool count varies by mailbox.
com.mailbox-mcp.toolsNote: This list is the mail surface, which every connected mailbox gets. The calendar and contact tools are absent: each is registered only on a mailbox whose owner has connected a diary or an address book, and Outlook contacts on a Microsoft mailbox that reconnects, so listing them here would be a promise the server had not kept. find_contact is on every mailbox; a connected book improves it. The summary says what each adds.
worksWith: Any IMAP and SMTP mail host
Microsoft 365 and Exchange Online, over OAuth
Gmail and Google Workspace, with an app password
Microsoft 365 and Google calendars, over OAuth

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.authentication: No API key required for rate-limited public access.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.availability: Public service backed by a connected compute worker. Calculations can be temporarily unavailable when that machine or its connection is offline. The separate contributor network depends on opted-in clients and exposes queued/expired states.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.privacy: The bounded public in-memory feed displays declared client name/version, tool, status and duration; identity is not authenticated. Operational aggregate metrics store no addresses, identities, inputs, results or Verify receipts. Retention: daily aggregates 90 UTC days; availability seven days; optional pricing email/plan/consent 30 days; private suggestions 90 days. No payment or marketing message is triggered. Contributor state, hosting/security logs and backups have separate rules at /privacy/. Never put secrets in clientInfo.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.summary: 35 independently callable MCP tools: 19 Rust scientific, six Discovery, six optional composition, three network and one Verify tool. Verify checks arithmetic, shadows, ephemerides, statistics and geometric routes, with model-scoped Ed25519 receipts; signatures do not establish physical truth or independent certification. Optimality claims differ from supplied-tour totals. Exact arithmetic uses checked rationals; unsupported floating-point paths remain inconclusive. Method Lab is bounded, train-only and never automatically promotes methods. Observation forecasts are conditional. Direct engines need no orchestrator. The typed bank has 22 capabilities and 46 fact contracts. CUDA supports simulate_pi and pi_chunk_v1. Contributor jobs are recomputed by the coordinator; no net distributed speedup is claimed.

environmentVariables.description: Editor WebSocket port. Default: the first Listen Ports entry in the project settings, else 8090.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_AUTOMATION_PORT

environmentVariables.description: Editor host to connect to. A LAN address also needs MCP_AUTOMATION_ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK=true and Allow Non Loopback in the plugin settings.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_AUTOMATION_HOST

environmentVariables.description: SECURITY: allow a non-loopback MCP_AUTOMATION_HOST. Enable only on a trusted network.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_AUTOMATION_ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK

environmentVariables.description: Connect with wss:// instead of ws://.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_AUTOMATION_USE_TLS

environmentVariables.description: Extra content roots to allow besides /Game, /Engine, /Script, /Temp and /Niagara, comma-separated. Example: /MyPluginContent/
environmentVariables.name: MCP_ADDITIONAL_PATH_PREFIXES

environmentVariables.description: How long to wait for the editor connection, in milliseconds.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS

environmentVariables.description: Overrides every per-capability request timeout, in milliseconds. Leave unset: each capability gets a budget that fits its cost.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS

environmentVariables.description: Inbound messages per minute from the editor before the server disconnects.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_AUTOMATION_MAX_MESSAGES_PER_MINUTE

environmentVariables.description: Log level. Logs go to stderr.
environmentVariables.name: LOG_LEVEL
